hook_text: In 1992, before South Africa was a democracy, a group of children wrote their own charter of rights. What did they ask for?
clip_script: Bloemfontein, Child Protection Week. Learners make posters: every child has the right to a name, to family care, to food and shelter, to be safe from abuse and to go to school. These rights are in the Constitution. In 1992, children from all over South Africa met in Cape Town and wrote the Children's Charter, asking for safety, education, equality and a voice. Rights come with responsibilities too.
visual_style: Whiteboard posters on a school wall with children's rights icons, then a hall full of children around tables writing a charter, then a two-column chart of rights and responsibilities.
mood: Warm and empowering, speaking directly to children about their own lives.
pacing: A lively poster opening, then a clear list of rights, then the story of the charter and the responsibilities.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write your own class charter with five rights and five responsibilities.
